topics.title: Vol II: Dispatch, Staging & Driving (205.02–205.11) (Part 1)
topics.sub: EMS dispatch, medical and rescue communications, hospital diversion, MCSO jail response, Deployment Sector, and overhaul rotation.
concepts: 205.02: Listed emergencies get the closest suppression unit plus a paramedic unit; all others get the nearest suppression unit only.
205.03: 1st Alarm Medical puts private helicopters and DPS Ranger on stand-by; disasters call Level 1 and specialty hospitals first.
205.04: Rescue Status 3 = fewer than 3 Rescues citywide; Channel 1 checks a Rescue at 20 minutes at the hospital; go available within 10 minutes of quarters.
205.04A: Uncontrollable airway/ventilation or no pulse goes to the closest appropriate facility regardless of diversion; Dispatch reconfirms in 3 hours.
205.05: Jail Assignment = ALS company, Rescue and BC; High-Risk benchmarks: entering, patient contact, extricated, PAR.
205.05A: The Dispatch Center Captain is Deployment Sector Officer and talks to Planning by telephone.
205.05B: Overhaul rotation uses the least active companies; companies that worked the fire stay off the list.

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.02, what is the basic philosophy behind the Phoenix EMS dispatch policy?
cards.a: An adequate, early and pessimistic response of the closest units required.
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: The policy "continues to revolve around an adequate, early and pessimistic response of the closest units required" to handle the emergency.
opts: Adequate, early and pessimistic response of the closest units
Minimum response first, upgraded only after patient contact
Closest paramedic unit only, with suppression units on request
Response based on the caller's own estimate of severity

cards.q: Dispatch receives a call for chest pain. Per M.P. 205.02, what is the standard dispatch?
cards.a: The closest fire suppression unit backed up by a paramedic unit.
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: Chest pain is on the list of emergencies that get "the closest fire suppression unit backed up by a paramedic unit."
opts: Closest suppression unit backed up by a paramedic unit
Nearest fire suppression unit only, to assess the patient
A Rescue only, with an engine added if requested
Two suppression units and a Battalion Chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.02, a call for a minor medical complaint not on the defined list receives what dispatch?
cards.a: The nearest fire suppression unit only, to assess, treat and decide on the need for ALS, Rescue or both.
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: Medical emergencies not defined in the list "will receive a dispatch of the nearest fire suppression unit only" to assess and determine the need for an ALS unit, Rescue or both.
opts: Nearest suppression unit only; it decides on ALS or Rescue
Closest suppression unit backed up by a paramedic unit, every time
A private ambulance only, with no fire unit assigned
Closest Rescue only, with an engine added if delayed

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.02, when a four-person paramedic unit is the closest unit to a listed emergency, who decides whether another company is sent?
cards.a: Dispatch personnel, based on their judgment and experience.
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: When a four-person paramedic unit is closest, "the dispatch of an additional company will be determined by the judgment/experience of the dispatch personnel."
opts: Dispatch personnel, using judgment and experience
The paramedic unit's Company Officer once on scene
The on-duty Battalion Chief for that area
No additional company is ever sent in that case

cards.q: A caller reports a 1-year-old who is failing to feed and has poor muscle tone. Per M.P. 205.02, how is this dispatched?
cards.a: As a listed emergency: closest suppression unit backed up by a paramedic unit (child under 18 months).
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: "Any child under 18 months" with dehydration, hypo/hyperthermia, poor muscle tone or failure to feed is on the list for suppression plus paramedic unit.
opts: Suppression unit plus paramedic unit, since the child is under 18 months
Nearest suppression unit only, since no trauma is reported
Suppression plus paramedic unit only if the child is under 6 months old
Rescue only, since pediatric calls go straight to transport

cards.q: Which of these auto accidents is specifically listed in M.P. 205.02 for a suppression unit plus paramedic dispatch?
cards.a: A car/bicycle accident.
cards.why: M.P. 205.02: Listed auto accidents include car/pedestrian, car/bicycle, motorcycle, and serious ones (rollover, person trapped).
opts: Car/bicycle collision
Two-car fender bender with no complaints
Single car into a parked car, driver walking
Minor parking lot collision at low speed

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.03, who upgrades the dispatched assignment on a medical incident when the actual situation requires it?
cards.a: Command.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: Dispatch sends an assignment based on reported scale; "the assignment will be upgraded by Command, as necessary, based on the actual situation encountered."
opts: Command
The Dispatch Center supervisor
The first arriving Rescue
The EMS Duty Officer

cards.q: On a 1st Alarm Medical, per M.P. 205.03, which resources does Dispatch place on stand-by?
cards.a: Private medical helicopters and the DPS Ranger.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: On a 1st Alarm Medical, Dispatch will "place private medical helicopters and DPS Ranger on stand-by."
opts: Private medical helicopters and DPS Ranger
All reserve Fire Department Rescues
Phoenix Transit buses at the Level 2 staging area
Level 2 hospitals by geographic proximity

cards.q: On a 2-1 Medical Assignment, per M.P. 205.03, which hospitals does Dispatch contact, and when?
cards.a: Level 1 and 2 hospitals, when requested by Command.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: For a 2-1 Medical, Dispatch will "contact Level 1 and 2 hospitals when requested by Command." (A 1st Alarm Medical lists Level 1 hospitals.)
opts: Level 1 and 2 hospitals, when requested by Command
Level 1 hospitals only, automatically at dispatch
Only the closest hospital, once patients are loaded
All hospitals in the valley, automatically at dispatch

cards.q: During a medical disaster notification per M.P. 205.03, which hospitals does Dispatch call first?
cards.a: All Level 1 hospitals and specialty hospitals; then Level 2 by proximity to the scene.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: "Call all Level 1 hospitals and specialty hospitals first. Call Level 2 facilities according to geographic proximity to scene."
opts: Level 1 and specialty hospitals, then Level 2 by proximity
The closest hospitals first, regardless of level
Level 2 hospitals first, to save Level 1 for critical patients
Only the hospitals that Transportation Sector names

cards.q: In a mass casualty notification per M.P. 205.03, what are hospitals told about calling the Dispatch Center?
cards.a: Not to call the Dispatch Center; stand by for a call back.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: Dispatch asks hospitals how many patients they can handle, to "stand-by for call back," and advises "them not to call the Dispatch Center."
opts: Not to call Dispatch; stand by for a call back
Call Dispatch every 15 minutes with bed counts
Call Transportation Sector directly on the tactical channel
Call Dispatch only when they reach capacity

cards.q: Command requests city buses at a medical disaster. Per M.P. 205.03, where does Dispatch send the Phoenix Transit buses?
cards.a: To the Level 2 staging area.
cards.why: M.P. 205.03: "Dispatch Phoenix Transit buses to the Level 2 staging area." The buses are radio dispatched.
opts: The Level 2 staging area
Directly to the Treatment Sector
The closest Level 1 hospital
The Command Post

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04, what is the minimum staffing of a fire department Rescue?
cards.a: Two fire fighters, each at least EMT certified or paramedic.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: "All fire department Rescues are staffed with a minimum of two fire fighters, which are at least EMT certified or EMT-P."
opts: Two fire fighters, at least EMT certified
Two paramedics, one of them a Captain
Three fire fighters, one of them a paramedic
One paramedic and one private EMT

cards.q: In the City of Phoenix, per M.P. 205.04, which call does NOT get a Rescue dispatched initially?
cards.a: A non-serious illness call (Rescues go initially only on GSW, stabbing, serious auto accident, car/ped, code and drowning).
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: In Phoenix a Rescue is sent initially on "gunshot wound, stabbing, auto accident that appears serious, car/pedestrian accident, code and drowning," or when a field unit requests one.
opts: A sick person with a minor illness
A car/pedestrian accident with minor injuries
A drowning
A stabbing

cards.q: A Phoenix Rescue is responding to an emergency with a response time over how many minutes before Dispatch checks for a closer private ambulance (M.P. 205.04)?
cards.a: 20 minutes.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: If a fire department Rescue's response time will exceed "20 minutes," the Dispatcher contacts private companies; if a closer private unit accepts, the FD Rescue is canceled.
opts: 20 minutes
10 minutes
15 minutes
30 minutes

cards.q: Your Rescue has been at the hospital about 20 minutes. Per M.P. 205.04, what happens?
cards.a: The Channel 1 operator contacts you to confirm status and when you expect to go available.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: "When a Rescue has been at the hospital for approximately 20 minutes, the Channel 1 operator will make contact with them to confirm their status."
opts: Channel 1 contacts you to confirm status and expected availability
You are automatically placed unavailable in CAD
The Dispatch Captain notifies your Battalion Chief of the delay at the ED
Nothing; status checks start at 45 minutes

cards.q: You're returning to your first due area after a transport. Per M.P. 205.04, when should your Rescue go available?
cards.a: When within 10 minutes driving time to quarters, monitoring Channel 1 en route.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: "Rescues should go available when within 10 minutes driving time to quarters" and monitor Channel 1 en route.
opts: Within 10 minutes driving time to quarters
Only once back in quarters (AIQ)
Within 20 minutes driving time to quarters
As soon as the patient is turned over

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04, what does Rescue Status 3 mean?
cards.a: An urgent call for ALL Rescues to return to service; fewer than three Rescues available citywide.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: Status 3 "is an urgent message for ALL Rescues to return to service" and is reserved for when "there are less than three Rescues available in the entire city."
opts: All Rescues return to service ASAP; fewer than 3 available citywide
A Rescue shortage in one area of the city, such as North or West
Fewer than five Rescues available; expedite turnarounds only
Private ambulances now handle all BLS transports

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04, Rescue Status 2 means a shortage in a particular area. Which area is defined as 'Central'?
cards.a: I-17 to 24th St, Bethany to I-10.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: Central is "I-17 to 24th St, Bethany to I-10"; North is north of Bethany, South is south of I-10, West is west of I-17, East is east of 24th St.
opts: I-17 to 24th St, Bethany to I-10
I-17 to 16th St, Northern to I-10
7th Ave to 24th St, Bethany to Buckeye
I-10 to 24th St, Camelback to I-17

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04, how many Rescues may be out of service at one time for scheduled activities like P.M., training or physicals?
cards.a: Two.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: "Only two Rescues will be allowed out-of-service at one time for scheduled activities." P.M.s should avoid 0700–0900 and 1500–1800.
opts: Two
One
Three
Four

cards.q: Your Rescue is leaving a hospital and Channel 1 tells you to take a new call. Per M.P. 205.04, what do you do first?
cards.a: Go available (AOR) from the previous call, then add unit (AU) to the new call once actually responding.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04: The Rescue "must first go available (AOR) from any previous call and add unit (AU) to the new call... DO NOT ADD YOURSELF TO THE CALL UNTIL ACTUALLY RESPONDING."
opts: Go AOR from the prior call, then AU when actually responding
AU to the new call right away, then clear the old call later
Ask the TRO to transfer your unit; no MCT entry is needed
Go AIQ, then wait for Dispatch to re-dispatch you

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04A, a patient has an uncontrollable airway problem. The closest appropriate ED is on diversion. Where does the patient go?
cards.a: To the closest appropriate facility regardless of hospital status.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04A: Patients with "uncontrollable medical problems shall be accepted by the closest appropriate facility regardless of hospital status."
opts: Closest appropriate facility, regardless of diversion
The nearest hospital that is open
Whichever open hospital on-line medical control directs
The nearest Level 1 trauma center

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04A, which is NOT an acceptable reason for a hospital to go on pre-hospital diversion?
cards.a: Saturation of critical care or medical beds alone.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04A: "At no time will saturation of critical care or medical beds alone be used as a reason to initiate pre-hospital diversion."
opts: Critical care or medical beds full, by itself
Emergency department saturation
Trauma service saturation
Internal disaster such as a power outage

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04A, what defines an 'uncontrollable medical problem' in a non-traumatic patient?
cards.a: Inability to provide an adequate airway or ventilation, or no palpable pulse.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04A: Uncontrollable medical problems are "the inability to provide an adequate airway or ventilation, lack of a palpable pulse, in the non-traumatic patient."
opts: No adequate airway or ventilation, or no palpable pulse
Systolic pressure under 90 with altered mentation
Any patient a paramedic rates as critical
Uncontrolled bleeding with signs of shock

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.04A, after a hospital notifies Dispatch of diversion, when does Dispatch follow up to reconfirm status?
cards.a: In three hours.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04A: The dispatcher will "follow-up with the affected hospital in three hours to reconfirm the status."
opts: Three hours
One hour
Six hours
At shift change

cards.q: Many valley hospitals are on diversion at once (system overload). Per M.P. 205.04A, what happens?
cards.a: All facilities must open; the EMS system may then be operating in a disaster mode.
cards.why: M.P. 205.04A: "When the entire system is overloaded (many facilities on diversion), all facilities must open."
opts: All facilities must open; system may be in disaster mode
Patients go to the least busy hospital in the region by rotation
Dispatch assigns hospitals by rotation
Only Level 1 trauma centers stay closed

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, what is the difference between a 'prisoner' and an 'inmate'?
cards.a: An inmate has been accepted into an MCSO jail and is in MCSO custody; a prisoner is still in the arresting agency's custody.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: A prisoner remains "in the custody of the arresting agency until accepted for confinement"; once accepted, the inmate "is now in the custody of MCSO."
opts: Inmate: accepted by MCSO; prisoner: still with arresting agency
Prisoner: accepted by MCSO; inmate: still with arresting agency
Inmate: sentenced by a court; prisoner: awaiting trial
No difference; the terms are used the same way

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, what makes up a Jail Assignment?
cards.a: An ALS fire company, a Rescue, and a Battalion Chief.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: "A Jail Assignment is an ALS fire company, Rescue, and a Battalion Chief."
opts: ALS fire company, Rescue and a Battalion Chief
Two ALS engines and a Rescue
ALS engine, ladder and a Rescue
BLS engine, Rescue and a Safety Officer

cards.q: You're dispatched to an MCSO jail. Per M.P. 205.05, when is the call upgraded to a Jail Assignment?
cards.a: When information consistently indicates the patient is in the High-Risk area.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: "If information on patient location consistently indicates patient is located in the High-Risk area, incident will be upgraded to a Jail Assignment."
opts: When the patient is consistently reported in the High-Risk area
Whenever the patient is an inmate rather than a prisoner of the arresting agency
When the patient is in the Medium-Risk medical area
Whenever CHS nurses have already started treatment

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, how is the Medium-Risk area defined at an MCSO jail?
cards.a: Inside any secured area, up to and including the predetermined medical evaluation areas.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: Medium-Risk is "the area inside any secured area, up to and including predetermined medical evaluation areas" agreed on by MCSO and PFD.
opts: Inside secured areas, up to the predetermined medical areas
Outside secured areas with reliable radio communication
Any area beyond the medical areas or with lost comms
Only the ITR booking area and the Sally Port

cards.q: Your crew is working inside a jail and loses radio communication. Per M.P. 205.05, what must the Company Officer do?
cards.a: Re-evaluate using the PFD risk management plan; a change of strategy and removal of crews may be required.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: "When communications are lost, the Company Officer must re-evaluate the incident utilizing the PFD risk management plan"; removal from the hazard area may be required.
opts: Re-evaluate with the risk plan; may change strategy and withdraw
Continue patient care and rely on the MCSO escort's radio
Request a second alarm and hold your position until communications return
Send one firefighter out to relay messages to FAHQ

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, before entering the High-Risk area, which benchmarks must be announced?
cards.a: Entering High-Risk area, patient contact, patient extricated, and PAR on crews.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: Benchmarks are "Entering High-Risk area," "Patient contact," "Patient extricated" and "PAR on crews."
opts: Entering High-Risk, patient contact, patient extricated, PAR
At sally port, at medical unit, patient loaded, leaving jail
Escort assigned, doors secured, patient contact, PAR
On scene, patient contact, transport started, available

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, which hospital should generally get first consideration for a patient in MCSO or law enforcement custody?
cards.a: Valleywise Health Medical Center (County Hospital).
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: "In most cases, Valleywise Health Medical Center (County Hospital/CH) should get first consideration" for patients in MCSO or other law enforcement custody.
opts: Valleywise Health Medical Center (County Hospital)
The closest Level 1 trauma center
The hospital CHS's Provider selects
The nearest open emergency department not on diversion

cards.q: An arresting agency declines to ride with a prisoner who now needs transport and you feel the person is a safety threat. Per M.P. 205.05, what do you do?
cards.a: Explain the concern and ask the arresting officer, as a professional courtesy, to ride along; if unwilling, request appropriate law enforcement.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: Medical personnel "should explain this to the arresting agency and request, as a professional courtesy, for the arresting officer to accompany them"; if unwilling, request appropriate law enforcement.
opts: Ask the officer to ride along; if refused, request law enforcement
Refuse transport until MCSO formally accepts custody of the prisoner
Transport anyway with the patient restrained by fire crews
Have CHS nurses accompany the patient in the Rescue

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05, after a jail response where a matter of concern arises, what does the crew complete?
cards.a: An Issue Tracker form, used by the Problem Resolution Team for quality review.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05: "An Issue Tracker form shall be completed by the responding crew" and used for quality review by the Problem Resolution Team.
opts: An Issue Tracker form for the Problem Resolution Team
An MCSO incident report through the jail Sergeant
A Safety Sector report to the Battalion Chief only
An exposure form sent to Correctional Health Services

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05A, who normally assumes the role of Deployment Sector Officer?
cards.a: The Captain in the Dispatch Center (the Dispatch and Deployment Supervisor in the Captain's absence).
cards.why: M.P. 205.05A: "The Captain in the Dispatch Center will assume the role of Deployment Sector Officer. In the Captain's absence, the Dispatch and Deployment Supervisor will assume this role."
opts: The Captain in the Dispatch Center
The Planning Section Chief at the scene
The on-duty Shift Commander
The first-due Battalion Chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05A, how does the Deployment Sector communicate with the Planning Section?
cards.a: By telephone, not a tactical radio channel.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05A: "Unlike most sectors, this sector will communicate directly with Planning via telephone rather than a tactical radio channel."
opts: By telephone instead of a tactical channel
On a dedicated tactical radio channel
Through the Command Post by MCT message on the incident
Through the Staging Sector Officer

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05A, which is a responsibility of the Deployment Sector?
cards.a: Maintaining adequate Regional coverage throughout the incident.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05A: Responsibilities include "Maintain adequate Regional coverage throughout the incident," assuring enough tactical channels, and re-evaluating emergency callback.
opts: Maintaining adequate Regional coverage during the incident
Assigning staged companies to sectors on scene for Command
Approving the Incident Action Plan for the IC
Tracking crew PARs on the fireground

cards.q: Dispatch is building an overhaul rotation list after a large fire. Per M.P. 205.05B, which companies should be chosen?
cards.a: Those with the least activity that day, after checking unit histories.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05B: "Unit histories should be checked for the day and companies that have had the least amount of activity should be selected."
opts: Least active companies of the day, per unit histories
Companies that worked the fire and know the building
Companies closest to the incident, regardless of activity
Multiple units from the same area to keep crews together

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05B, should a company that worked a substantial time at the fire be put on the overhaul rotation list?
cards.a: No, it should not be placed on the rotation list.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05B: "Any company that participated for a substantial period of time at the incident should not be placed on the rotation list."
opts: No, it should not be on the rotation list
Yes, it should take the first rotation
Yes, but only if the IC requests it by name
Only if it has been out of service less than 4 hours

cards.q: An outlying company is selected for overhaul rotation. Per M.P. 205.05B, who should cover its area?
cards.a: An adaptive response unit not used on the incident.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05B: "When an outlying company is selected for rotation, an adaptive response unit not used on the incident should cover for that company."
opts: An adaptive response unit not used on the incident
The company being relieved from the fire, once it is back in service
A reserve engine staffed on callback
The neighboring first-due company

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.05B, what must advance notice to rotation companies include, when possible?
cards.a: Time to respond, duration of the assignment, and who their relief will be.
cards.why: M.P. 205.05B: "Notification will include the time to respond, the duration of their assignment and who their relief will be."
opts: Time to respond, assignment length, and their relief
The IC's name, tactical channel, and staging location
Equipment list, fire cause, and the overhaul sector
Only the time to respond; details come on scene

topics.title: Vol II: Dispatch, Staging & Driving (205.02–205.11) (Part 2)
topics.sub: Staging Sector, apparatus placement, safe parking in traffic, Code 3 driving, spotting, escorts, adaptive response, ladder and water tenders.
concepts: 205.06A: No designated Staging Officer: the first company to staging takes it (a ladder hands off to an engine officer).
205.07: Later companies stage at least one block short; apparatus at least 30 ft from involved buildings.
205.07A: Angle 45 degrees, pump panel downstream; nighttime headlights off; cones 65/105/160 ft at 25/40/60 mph.
205.08: Code 3 max 10 mph over posted, 20 mph in center/oncoming lanes with a full stop at every controlled intersection.
205.08A: Primary spotter at left rear, 10–15 ft back; lose sight of the spotter and you stop.
205.08B: The on-scene Company Officer makes the final escort decision; escorts wear seat belts.
205.09: ARU move-ups are normally Code 2, out of service responding, monitoring Channel One.
205.10/205.11: Full crew on the Ladder Truck for 3-1 or greater; water tenders go with the engine, never Code 3.

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.06A, which incidents should use Level II staging?
cards.a: All greater alarm incidents, first alarm medical or hazmat incidents, or whenever Command wants to centralize resources.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: Level II "should be utilized for all greater alarm incidents, first alarm medical or hazardous materials incidents," or when Command wants to centralize resources.
opts: Greater alarms, 1st alarm medical or hazmat, or as Command wants
Only greater alarm structure fires of 3 alarms or more
Every first alarm assignment, including routine single-family fires
Only incidents where a Logistics Section is in place

cards.q: Level II staging is set up but Command didn't name a Staging Officer. Per M.P. 205.06A, who becomes the Staging Officer?
cards.a: The first company to arrive at the designated staging location.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: "Where an officer is not designated, the first company to arrive at the designated staging location will automatically become the staging officer."
opts: The first company to arrive at the staging location
The last-due engine company on the assignment
The first Battalion Chief to arrive on scene
The company closest to the Command Post

cards.q: Your ladder company is first into Level II staging. Per M.P. 205.06A, what happens to the Staging Sector job?
cards.a: You take it, then transfer it to an engine company officer when one arrives.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: "Where the first company to staging is a ladder company, Staging Sector responsibilities should be transferred to an engine company officer upon his arrival."
opts: Transfer it to an engine company officer when one arrives
Keep it for the rest of the incident
Transfer it to the first Rescue or Battalion Chief that arrives
Decline it; ladders cannot be Staging Sector

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.06A, how does the Staging Officer make the position visible to incoming companies?
cards.a: Leaves the red lights on their apparatus operating and wears a sector vest.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: Visibility is accomplished "by leaving the red lights operating on the staging officers apparatus and by wearing a sector vest."
opts: Red lights left on the apparatus and a sector vest
Amber lights only and a reflective traffic vest
A cone and flare marker at the staging entrance
Headlights off and the scene lights aimed at the lot

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.06A, how should apparatus be organized in the staging area?
cards.a: Ladders in one area, engines in another, and rescues in another, with adequate space between them.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: "Ladders companies should be placed in one area, engines in another, and rescues in another area," with adequate space for movement.
opts: Ladders, engines and rescues each grouped in their own area
In order of arrival, in a single line for quick exit
By home battalion, so crews stay together
Rescues closest to the scene exit, all other apparatus mixed in behind

cards.q: Command needs only extra staff and some special equipment at the scene. Per M.P. 205.06A, what should Staging do?
cards.a: Set up a 'taxi' service, using a single company to deliver multiple crews or equipment.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: Staging "should arrange a 'taxi' service using a single company to deliver multiple crews or specialized equipment to the scene" to minimize congestion.
opts: Use one company as a 'taxi' for crews and equipment
Send each staff member's own vehicle to the scene
Send the equipment's home company with its apparatus
Ask Logistics to set up a second staging area

cards.q: During a major incident with a Logistics Section in place, per M.P. 205.06A, who does the Staging Sector work under?
cards.a: The Logistics Officer.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: "During major incidents where a 'Logistics' Section is implemented, the Staging Sector will be working under the direction of the Logistics Officer."
opts: The Logistics Officer
The Planning Section Chief
The Deployment Sector Officer
The Safety Officer

cards.q: Staging assigns your company to a sector. Per M.P. 205.06A, what do you do with the MCT?
cards.a: Activate the MCT "on-scene" button.
cards.why: M.P. 205.06A: "When assigned to incident site duties, companies will activate their MCT 'on-scene' button."
opts: Press the MCT on-scene button
Press the MCT available button
Leave the MCT in staged status
Press the MCT responding button

cards.q: You're the third engine arriving at a working house fire. Per M.P. 205.07, where should you go if not given an assignment?
cards.a: Stage at least one block short of the fire area, uncommitted until Command orders you in.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Later arriving companies should stage a minimum of one block short of the immediate fire area, and remain uncommitted until ordered into action by Command."
opts: At least one block short, uncommitted, until Command assigns you
Pull in right behind the first engine to back up its attack lines
Go to the nearest hydrant and lay a supply line in
Report to Level II staging two blocks away

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07, how far from an involved building should apparatus generally be positioned, even with nothing showing?
cards.a: At least 30 feet, with greater distances indicated in many situations.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Apparatus should generally be positioned at least 30 ft. away from involved buildings, even with nothing showing."
opts: At least 30 feet
At least 15 feet
At least 50 feet
At least 100 feet

cards.q: Fire is threatening your parked engine. Per M.P. 205.07, what do you do while you reposition it?
cards.a: Activate the engine sprinkler system and operate hoselines between it and the fire.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Activate engine sprinkler system and operate hoselines between it and the fire while you reposition it," then move it to a safe position.
opts: Activate the engine sprinkler and put hoselines between it and fire
Shut down the pump and move it before charging any lines
Leave it in place; moving apparatus mid-fire is dysfunctional
Wrap the cab in a salvage cover and request a new engine

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07, what is the minimum water supply for an engine in a key tactical position?
cards.a: At least one pumped line from an engine on a hydrant (two when high volume is indicated).
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "The water supply should be at least one pumped line from an engine on a hydrant. When high volume is indicated, two pumped supply lines should be provided."
opts: One pumped line from an engine on a hydrant
Its own tank water until a second alarm arrives
Two unpumped lines from the closest hydrant
One forward lay from a hydrant, no pumper needed

cards.q: You need more handlines at a fire. Per M.P. 205.07, what should you do instead of 'daisy chain' supply connections?
cards.a: Connect the extra lines to pumpers that already have a good supply line.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Connect extra lines to pumpers which already have a good supply line instead of making 'daisy chain' supply line connections."
opts: Connect to pumpers already on a good supply line
Bring in another engine to a distant hydrant
Have each new engine lay its own supply line
Relay pump through two engines in series

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07, when the aerial is not needed for upper access or rescue, how should the ladder be spotted?
cards.a: In a position for effective elevated stream operation if the fire goes defensive.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: Spot the ladder "in a position that would provide an effective position for elevated stream operation if the fire goes to a defensive mode."
opts: Where it can run an elevated stream if the fire goes defensive
Out of the way at least one block from the fire
Next to the Command vehicle for visibility
Directly behind the first engine so it can share that engine's water supply

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07, where do staff vehicles go on the fireground?
cards.a: To Level II staging, unless the staff person has a pre-designated job such as Safety Sector.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Staff vehicle placement should go to Level II staging unless that staff person has a pre-designated responsibility (i.e., Safety Sector)."
opts: Level II staging, unless pre-assigned such as Safety Sector
Next to the Command vehicle at the Command Post
Anywhere close to the fire that does not block the center access lane
Level I staging one block short of the fire

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07, which positions should you beware of for fire apparatus?
cards.a: Places with only one way in and out, such as yards, alleys and driveways.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07: "Beware of putting fire apparatus in places where it cannot be repositioned easily and quickly--particularly operating positions with only one way in and out."
opts: Spots with one way in and out, like yards and alleys
Positions on the same side of the street as the hydrant
Spots with clear views of two sides of the building
Positions at corners that cover two sides of the fire

cards.q: You pull up to a car crash on a city street. Per M.P. 205.07A, how should the engine be angled where possible?
cards.a: At 45 degrees away from the curbside, to direct motorists around the scene.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "Where possible, angle apparatus at 45 degrees away from curbside. This will direct motorist around the scene."
opts: 45 degrees away from the curbside
90 degrees across all lanes of traffic
Parallel to the curb, in front of the scene
30 degrees toward the curbside

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07A, when a first-arriving engine may need a charged line at a roadway scene, where should the pump panel be?
cards.a: Downstream, on the side opposite oncoming traffic.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "Angle the engine so that the pump panel is 'downstream,' on the opposite side of on-coming traffic. This will protect the pump operator."
opts: Downstream, away from oncoming traffic
Upstream, facing oncoming traffic
Toward the curb, whatever the traffic flow
Toward the center median

cards.q: It's 0200 and you're blocking at a roadway crash. Per M.P. 205.07A, what lighting should the apparatus use?
cards.a: Headlights OFF; reduce other emergency lighting to yellow lights and flashers where possible.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "For NIGHTTIME operations, turn OFF fire apparatus headlights." Other lighting "should be reduced to yellow lights and emergency flashers where possible."
opts: Headlights off; reduce to yellow lights and flashers
All emergency lights and headlights on full
Headlights on high beam aimed at oncoming traffic
All lights off except the scene floodlights

cards.q: On a 40 mph street, per M.P. 205.07A, where should traffic cones and flares start?
cards.a: About 105 feet.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: Recommended starting distances are 25 mph – 65 ft, 40 mph – 105 ft, 60 mph – 160 ft.
opts: 105 feet
65 feet
160 feet
200 feet

cards.q: You're on a freeway crash. Per M.P. 205.07A, about how far upstream should the last traffic cone be?
cards.a: About 160 feet upstream.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: On freeways cones are placed farther apart, "with the last cone approximately 160 feet 'upstream.'"
opts: About 160 feet
About 105 feet
About 65 feet
About 300 feet

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07A, how should you place and retrieve traffic cones?
cards.a: While facing oncoming traffic.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "Always place and retrieve cones while facing on-coming traffic."
opts: Facing oncoming traffic
With your back to oncoming traffic
Only from inside the blocked lane
Only after police have stopped traffic

cards.q: At a freeway incident, per M.P. 205.07A, how are Rescues brought into the scene?
cards.a: One or two at a time, possibly staged off the freeway, into a safe loading area.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "Staging of Rescue companies off the freeway may be required. Rescues should be brought into the scene one or two at a time."
opts: One or two at a time to a safe loading area
All at once so patients can be loaded quickly
Only after DPS shuts down the freeway
Directly behind the blocking engine, upstream

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.07A, who must direct the parking of later-arriving apparatus at a roadway scene?
cards.a: The initial company officer (or Command), acting as initial safety officer.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "The initial company officer (or Command) must assess the parking needs of later-arriving fire apparatus and specifically direct the parking."
opts: The initial company officer or Command
Each later-arriving company officer for themselves
The first police officer on scene
The first-arriving Rescue's crew

cards.q: At a residential medical call, per M.P. 205.07A, where should the Rescue park for loading when possible?
cards.a: In the driveway.
cards.why: M.P. 205.07A: "At residential medical emergencies, park Rescue in driveways for safe loading where possible."
opts: In the driveway
In the street behind the engine
Across the street, facing out
Upstream of the engine as a blocker

cards.q: You're driving E1 Code 3 with traffic on a 40 mph road. Per M.P. 205.08, what is your maximum speed?
cards.a: 50 mph (10 mph over the posted limit).
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: Code 3 standards allow a "maximum of 10 mph over the posted speed limit."
opts: 50 mph
45 mph
55 mph
60 mph

cards.q: You're driving Code 3 in the oncoming lane to get around stopped traffic. Per M.P. 205.08, what is the maximum speed?
cards.a: 20 mph.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: "A maximum of 20 mph when traveling in center or oncoming traffic lanes," recognizing a brief deceleration period.
opts: 20 mph
15 mph
25 mph
10 mph over posted

cards.q: Code 3 in the center lane, you approach an intersection with a green light. Per M.P. 205.08, what do you do?
cards.a: Come to a complete stop before proceeding, even on a green light.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: In center or oncoming lanes, "complete a stop at all stop signs and traffic lights regardless of the color of the light."
opts: Complete stop, even with the green light
Slow to 20 mph and proceed on the green
Proceed at the posted limit on the green
Slow down and proceed if the co-driver says clear

cards.q: You're Code 3 and use a left-turn lane to get past traffic. Per M.P. 205.08, when may you go without stopping?
cards.a: Only when turning left under a protected green arrow.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: A left-turn lane is treated as an oncoming lane; "the only exception is when the left-hand turn lane is being used to execute a left turn under a protected green arrow."
opts: Only when turning left on a protected green arrow
Whenever the main signal ahead is green
Whenever no vehicles are already in the turn lane
Never; you must always stop in a left-turn lane

cards.q: Code 3, you come up on a school bus with its stop sign out. Per M.P. 205.08, what do you do?
cards.a: Stop completely and wait until the sign is retracted and the driver and co-driver confirm pedestrians are clear.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: Stop and "not proceed until the stop sign is fully retracted or removed and all pedestrian traffic is confirmed clear by both the Driver and Co-driver."
opts: Stop; wait for sign retracted and both confirm peds clear
Slow to 10 mph and pass with lights and siren on
Stop, then pass once the bus driver waves you on
Pass at or below the posted speed if no children are visible near the bus

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08, at a Code 3 stop, who announces 'clear' and who makes the final decision to proceed?
cards.a: The co-driver announces clear or not clear; the driver makes the final decision.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: "The Co-driver shall announce if it is clear or not clear to proceed. The Driver makes the final decision of when it is clear to proceed."
opts: Co-driver announces clear; driver makes the final call
Driver announces clear; Company Officer gives the go
Co-driver announces clear and makes the final call
Driver decides alone; co-driver watches the MCT

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08, if no response code is designated on the MCT, how do you respond?
cards.a: Code 2, unless directed otherwise by a Company Officer.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: "If no response code is designated, the response will be Code 2 unless directed by a Company Officer."
opts: Code 2 unless a Company Officer directs otherwise
Code 3 until the Alarm Room says otherwise
Code 3 for ALS calls and Code 2 for BLS calls
Hold in quarters until the Alarm Room assigns one

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08, which apparatus is not permitted to respond Code 3 at all?
cards.a: Water Tenders.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: "Water Tenders are not permitted to respond Code 3."
opts: Water Tenders
Ladder Tenders
Rescues on BLS calls
Utility units

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08, which is an example of a MAJOR policy deviation that goes through the disciplinary process?
cards.a: Going through a controlled intersection without stopping when required, or exceeding allowed speed by 10 mph or more.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: Momentarily exceeding max speed by "5 mph or less" is minor; going through a controlled intersection without stopping or exceeding "by 10 mph or more" is major.
opts: Running a required stop, or 10+ mph over the allowed speed
Momentarily exceeding the allowed speed by 5 mph or less
Not pressing the MCT response code button
Using Code 3 in an active school zone

cards.q: During a transport, your patient's condition requires you to unbuckle for critical treatment. Per M.P. 205.08, what's the first choice?
cards.a: Tell the driver, who pulls over when possible so you can treat, then re-buckle before continuing.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08: "The Driver will be notified of the needed treatment and will pull over when possible." Treating unbelted while moving is for life-threatening needs.
opts: Tell the driver to pull over when possible, then treat
Unbuckle and treat right away; the driver does not need to be told
Wait until arrival at the hospital to treat
Have the driver go Code 3 so you arrive sooner

cards.q: You need to back the engine into quarters. Per M.P. 205.08A, where is the primary spotter usually located?
cards.a: At the left rear corner of the apparatus.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: "The primary spotter is usually located at the left rear corner of the apparatus," though position follows the agreed backing plan.
opts: Left rear corner
Right rear corner
Directly behind the center of the rig
Beside the driver's door

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08A, how far behind the apparatus should rear spotters stay?
cards.a: About 10–15 feet, where they can see the driver's eyes in the side mirror.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: "Rear spotters will remain a reasonably safe distance (10-15 feet) behind the apparatus and be in position to visualize the driver's eyes in the side mirror."
opts: 10–15 feet
3–5 feet
20–25 feet
30 feet or more

cards.q: You're the only person on the apparatus and must back up. Per M.P. 205.08A, what do you do if no one is available to spot?
cards.a: Get out and make a complete 360-degree survey around the apparatus first.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: Where no personnel are available, "the driver shall get out of the apparatus and make a complete 360-degree survey of the area around the apparatus."
opts: Get out and do a full 360-degree walk-around
Back slowly using mirrors and the backup camera
Ask a bystander to spot and use hand signals
Back only with emergency lights and horn on

cards.q: While backing, the driver loses sight of the primary spotter. Per M.P. 205.08A, what must happen?
cards.a: Stop immediately until the spotter is visible again and the go-ahead is given.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: "Anytime the driver loses sight of the primary spotter, the apparatus shall be stopped immediately until the spotter is visible."
opts: Stop at once until the spotter is visible and gives the go
Keep backing slowly while watching the other mirror for the spotter
Sound the horn and continue if the radio is quiet
Watch the second spotter and keep going

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08A, what is the STOP signal for a spotter?
cards.a: Both arms crossed with hands making a fist, while yelling the stop order loud enough to hear.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: STOP is "both arms crossed with hands making a fist. Be sure to yell the stop order loud enough that the engineer/driver can hear."
opts: Arms crossed with fists, and yell stop
Both palms facing the driver, held still
One fist raised straight overhead
Arms out wide, then brought together

cards.q: Backing at night, per M.P. 205.08A, how should spotters signal the driver?
cards.a: With hand signals lit by the apparatus floodlights; never with flashlights.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08A: Floodlights should light objects and the spotter's location; "the spotters should never use flashlights to signal the driver."
opts: Hand signals lit by the floodlights; no flashlights
With flashlights aimed at the driver's mirror
By portable radio only, with lights off
With light sticks waved in the agreed direction

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08B, who makes the final decision on whether an escort rides with the patient in the Rescue?
cards.a: The Company Officer on scene.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08B: Rescue crews discuss the considerations with the on-scene officer, and "the Company Officer on scene will make the final decision."
opts: The Company Officer on scene
The Rescue's lead paramedic attendant
The Rescue's driver
On-line medical control

cards.q: A family member wants to ride along but smells strongly of alcohol and is agitated. Per M.P. 205.08B, what's the right call?
cards.a: Escort is not advised (possible physical danger); offer other transportation options.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08B: Signs of "behavioral stress, or possible alcohol or drug intoxication" are reasons to refuse; provide info on taxis, private cars, buses, etc.
opts: Refuse the escort and offer other transportation options
Allow it if they sit in the front cab with the driver
Allow it only if a police officer rides along too
Allow it; family escorts can't be refused

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08B, who should NOT ride in a Rescue cab with airbags installed?
cards.a: Small adults or young children.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08B: "Small adults or young children should not ride in any rescue cab with airbags installed." Seat belts are mandatory for escorts.
opts: Small adults or young children
Pregnant escorts
Escorts over 65 years old
Anyone not related to the patient

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.08B, which is listed as a good reason to allow an escort?
cards.a: The escort can translate a second language (e.g., Spanish or ASL) to help patient care.
cards.why: M.P. 205.08B: Patient care examples include "an escort who has the knowledge of a second language, i.e., Spanish, American Sign Language."
opts: They can translate a second language for patient care
They want to save the cost of a taxi
They need a ride to the same hospital area
They want to watch and supervise the crew's treatment of the patient

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.09, how do Adaptive Response Units normally respond to a move-up assignment?
cards.a: Code 2, in an 'out of service' responding status while monitoring Channel One.
cards.why: M.P. 205.09: "Move-ups will normally be under a non-emergency Code 2 status," in an "out of service" responding status while monitoring Channel One.
opts: Code 2, out-of-service responding, monitoring Channel One
Code 3, in service and available for any call
Code 2, in service and available for all calls
Code 3 whenever the first-due unit is committed on a working fire

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.09, who is responsible for managing adaptive response move-ups?
cards.a: The AHQ Chief, Alarm Room Supervisors and Lead Dispatchers.
cards.why: M.P. 205.09: "The AHQ Chief, Alarm Room Supervisors, and Lead Dispatchers are responsible for management of adaptive response move-ups."
opts: AHQ Chief, Alarm Room Supervisors and Lead Dispatchers
The field Battalion Chiefs in each affected area
The Shift Commander alone
The company officers of the covering units

cards.q: Your ARU is covering another station and the covered company's activity has ended. Per M.P. 205.09, when do you leave?
cards.a: Stay in the move-up location (in service) until dispatched by alarm to return or move.
cards.why: M.P. 205.09: ARUs "shall stay in their move-up location (in service) until assigned dispatched by alarm to return to their first due or another location."
opts: Stay until alarm dispatches you back or elsewhere
Return to quarters once the covered company is back
Return after the 2-hour move-up time limit
Leave when your Company Officer decides coverage is done

cards.q: Your ARU has a problem with a move-up. Per M.P. 205.09, who does the Company Officer take it to?
cards.a: Their BC (not AHQ); an Issue Tracker in EPCR is also an option.
cards.why: M.P. 205.09: Company Officers "shall communicate any issues associated with BC and not AHQ" and may submit an issue tracker in EPCR.
opts: Their BC, not AHQ
The AHQ Supervisor directly
The Shift Commander directly
The Lead Dispatcher on Channel One

cards.q: A move-up will send your company out of its city (e.g., into Glendale). Per M.P. 205.09, who should be notified?
cards.a: The appropriate Shift Commander.
cards.why: M.P. 205.09: "When a move-up requires a company to leave their city (i.e.: Glendale), the appropriate Shift Commander should be notified."
opts: The appropriate Shift Commander
The receiving city's Fire Chief
The Deployment Sector Officer
The Operations Chief

cards.q: Your crew is in quarters when a 3-1 structure fire comes in. Per M.P. 205.10, which apparatus does the crew take?
cards.a: The Ladder Truck with a complete crew; the officer may also bring the Ladder Tender.
cards.why: M.P. 205.10: From quarters, "a complete crew will respond on the Ladder Truck to all structural assignments of 3-1 or greater magnitude."
opts: The Ladder Truck; the Ladder Tender may come too
The Ladder Tender, since it's faster to deploy
Whichever unit the driver is most familiar with
The Ladder Tender, with the truck special-called

cards.q: You're out of quarters in the Ladder Tender and get a structure fire. Per M.P. 205.10, what do you do?
cards.a: Respond in the Ladder Tender and advise Dispatch; request a backup Ladder Truck if any indicator suggests it isn't adequate.
cards.why: M.P. 205.10: Respond in the LT, "Dispatch must be advised," and "if any indicators suggest that the apparatus may not be adequate... a backup Ladder Truck should be requested."
opts: Respond in the LT, advise Dispatch, request a truck if in doubt
Return to quarters to switch to the Ladder Truck
Go out of service and let Dispatch send another ladder company instead
Respond in the LT; no notification is needed

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.10, what minimum crew may a two-piece truck company put on the Ladder Tender for a BLS dispatch?
cards.a: Four members.
cards.why: M.P. 205.10: The officer "may choose to respond to a B.L.S. dispatch with a minimum four-member crew on the Ladder Tender."
opts: Four
Two
Three
Five

cards.q: Per M.P. 205.11, can a company with a water tender take the tender in place of its engine?
cards.a: No; it may take the tender with its engine (not in lieu of) when water supply is limited.
cards.why: M.P. 205.11: Officers "can take the water tender with their engine (but not in lieu of) when the water tender is needed due to limited water supply."
opts: No; only with the engine, when water supply is limited
Yes, whenever the officer thinks it's appropriate
Yes, but only on brush fires
Yes, if Dispatch approves the swap

cards.q: Command special-calls a water tender 'driver only.' Per M.P. 205.11, who assigns the driver?
cards.a: The Company Officer assigns a qualified driver/pump operator.
cards.why: M.P. 205.11: "When a water tender is requested with a driver only, the Company officer is responsible to assign a qualified driver/pump operator."
opts: The Company Officer, choosing a qualified driver/pump operator
The Alarm Room, choosing an engineer from the constant manning list
Command, by naming a specific engineer
The Battalion Chief of the tender's station

cards.q: Engine 30's crew picks up a water tender housed at another station. Per M.P. 205.11, how is the tender identified?
cards.a: It keeps its home station identification (e.g., 'Engine 30 responding with water tender ( )').
cards.why: M.P. 205.11: "The water tender will always retain its home station identification regardless of the assigned crews."
opts: It keeps its home station's identification
It takes Engine 30's number
It is renamed by the Alarm Room
It goes by the Command-assigned sector name

notes: No 205.06 (Level I/Level II Staging) text file exists in build/mp-text; only 205.06A Staging Sector was available, so Level I/II staging is covered only as 205.06A and 205.07 describe it.
205.02 (10/97) numbers two different list items '22' (auto accidents and 'any other medical emergency'); the second is presumably 24.

205.03 and 205.05A (10/97), 205.04 (03/03), 205.04A (07/99), 205.05B (05/95), 205.07 and 205.11 (01/95) are old revisions; dispatch names (Channel 1, DS2, TRO) and the 205.04 list of contract cities may be out of date.
205.03 gives 2-1 Medical as 'Level 1 and 2 hospitals' but 1st Alarm Medical as 'Level 1 hospitals'; carded as written.
205.05 location illustrations, 205.05A org chart and 205.07A figures 1–8 are images and did not extract; cards use the text only.
